name: IL-16
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+11 district lean strongly favors the incumbent party
LaHood holds a roughly 10-to-1 cash advantage ($6.3M vs $230K)
Markets price the race about 96% Republican and no polling shows a contest
A Democratic-tilted national environment is Nolley's main asset
model.rationale: An eleven-point Republican lean, LaHood's overwhelming fundraising edge, and market pricing near 96 percent Republican leave Nolley without a visible path; the lone offsetting evidence is a national environment favoring Democrats, which is not nearly enough on its own.
model.watch: The forecast would move only if polling emerged showing the race in single digits or an unusually large national Democratic wave developed in the final weeks.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
IL-16 is a safely Republican seat in central Illinois, with a partisan lean of roughly eleven points toward the GOP. Incumbent Darin LaHood enters the general election after renomination with a dominant financial position: about $4.2 million raised and $6.3 million on hand. Democratic nominee Paul Nolley has raised roughly $416 thousand, leaving him outspent around ten to one, with essentially no outside spending on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings track the race, and betting markets put Republican win odds near 96 percent. The main counterweight for Democrats is a national environment that has leaned their way this cycle, but even a sizable swing would need to overcome the district's Republican lean and a well-funded, entrenched incumbent. The forecast calls this seat safely Republican.
